summary: As of November 5, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.48 percentage points, +0.22 percentage points over five trading days, and the junk-versus-safe gap is 2.55 percentage points. VIX is 28.18 and the 3-month VIX is 25.55, so near-term fear is above the 3-month reading. The Nasdaq-100 is -14.8 percent from its trailing high, semiconductors are -14.1 percent versus their 200-day average, and 63 percent of the 30-name list is above its own 200-day average.
what_would_change_this: The headline would leave risk-on if junk spreads reached 4.50 percentage points, near-term volatility rose above the 3-month reading by more than half a point, or the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10 percent below its trailing high.
what_the_tape_is_saying: As of November 5, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.48 percentage points and are up 0.22 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.04 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.07 percentage points. Of the 0.08 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.22 was the credit spread and 0.14 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 4.90 percent as of November 4, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.28 percent as of November 4, 2026, a gap of 0.38 percentage points. Brent is 99.29 dollars a barrel as of November 5, 2026 (-13.57 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.26 percent as of November 5, 2026, down 0.21 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.64 percent as of November 4, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.67 as of October 30, 2026, -0.12 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 28.18 as of November 5, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.75 trillion dollars as of November 4, 2026, up 1 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.93 trillion dollars as of November 4, 2026, down 100 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.125 billion dollars as of November 5, 2026, down 4.2 billion over the latest four observations.
